item.title: PM for sustainable housing sector, balanced urban development
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday said the government is committed to building a transparent, accountable and investment-friendly environment for sustainable, planned and corruption-free development of the housing sector.
During a meeting with a delegation of the Real Estate and Housing Association of Bangladesh (REHAB) at the Secretariat, he also said planned and sustainable urbanization is essential for Bangladesh's long-term economic growth, said a release issued by the prime minister’s Press Wing.
The prime minister stressed that urban development should not remain Dhaka-centric, urging greater emphasis on balanced development across the country while protecting agricultural land.
At the meeting, the REHAB delegation discussed the current state of the housing industry, challenges to planned urbanization, practical difficulties arising from the implementation of the Detailed Area Plan (DAP), and measures needed for the sector's long-term development.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman meets a delegation of the Real Estate and Housing Association of Bangladesh (REHAB) at the Secretariat on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. Photo: PM’s Press Wing
The association proposed reducing land, plot and apartment registration fees to a reasonable level to encourage investment in the housing sector.
The delegation also called for the complete digitalisation of government services related to the real estate sector to improve efficiency and transparency.
The REHAB leaders urged the government to rationally increase the Floor Area Ratio (FAR) and promote vertical urban development to ensure the best use of limited land, particularly in the capital.
Addressing the delegation, Tarique Rahman described the housing sector as one of the key drivers of the national economy.
"The development of the housing sector is vital for the country's overall economic growth. The government is working to establish a transparent, accountable and investment-friendly environment where the housing industry can grow in a planned, sustainable and corruption-free manner," he said.
The prime minister said the government has already undertaken a series of reform initiatives to prevent irregularities in the housing sector and that further effective measures are being prepared.
He also emphasized the need to expand planned urbanisation beyond Dhaka.
"Urban development should not remain centred only on Dhaka. Other regions of the country must also be developed in a planned manner with equal importance," Tarique Rahman said, adding that agricultural land must be protected alongside development activities.
Housing and Public Works Minister Zakaria Taher attended the meeting along with REHAB President Dr Ali Afzal, Vice-President-2 Abu Khalid Md Barkatullah and senior representatives of leading real estate companies, including Eastern Housing Ltd, United Group, Rupayan Group, Amin Mohammad Group, Century Group, US-Bangla Assets Ltd and Swadesh Properties Ltd.

item.title: Fakhrul: Local polls likely by year-end or early 2027
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Wednesday said local government elections are likely to be held either by the end of this year or in early 2027, assuring that the polls will be conducted in a free, fair and impartial manner without any political interference.
Speaking as the chief guest at a discussion organized by the Bangladesh Union Parishad Chairmen and Members Association at the auditorium of the Institution of Diploma Engineers, Bangladesh, he said there will be no scope for anyone to influence the elections and that candidates will have to secure victory through the people's support.
Addressing UP chairmen and members, Fakhrul, also BNP secretary general, said elected representatives regularly participate in the festivals of people from different faiths and stressed that communal harmony must be preserved.
Referring to the upcoming local government elections, he said no political party – BNP or Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami – will receive any special privilege. "Chairmen, members and women members will have to be elected through the people's support. This is the true foundation of democracy," he said.
The minister also stressed the need for proper distribution of relief so that the rights of the poor are not violated.
He said a country's democracy and state system become truly strong only when its local government system is effective and empowered, noting that empowering grassroots public representatives will help deliver services to people's doorsteps and further strengthen the foundation of democracy.
Fakhrul said local governments in developed countries serve as the foundation of administration, justice, healthcare and various public services.
"But since independence, Bangladesh has not been able to bring its local government system to that desired level of strength. Now is the time to empower local government in the true sense," he said.
The minister described UP chairmen and members as the closest representatives of the people at the grassroots who understand local problems, needs, and opportunities better than anyone else, pledging to discuss their allowances with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to ensure they receive a more respectable level of benefits.
He underscored the need for making local government more effective and stronger to institutionalize development and democracy.
Fakhrul said local representatives should be involved in determining beneficiaries of various government programs, including social safety net initiatives.
He also called for greater empowerment of women and improvements in the country's education system, saying Bangladesh will not be able to move forward without educational advancement.
The minister said healthcare services should also be brought closer to local government institutions so they can play a greater role in improving public health services.

Technical fault at FSRU disrupts gas supply
item.description:
The government on Wednesday said a technical fault at one of the country’s Floating Storage and Regasification Units (FSRUs) has disrupted gas supply to the national grid, reducing daily gas supply by around 450 million cubic feet (mmcfd) and affecting industries, power plants and compressed natural gas (CNG) stations.
The Energy and Mineral Resources Division in a statement said gas regasification from the affected FSRU has been suspended due to the technical problem.
As a result, gas pressure has dropped in several parts of the country, causing disruptions to industrial production, electricity generation and CNG refueling operations, it added.
In some areas, CNG stations have been unable to receive the required volume of gas, leading to long queues and public inconvenience.
Engineers and technical experts are working on the highest priority basis to restore normal operations at the FSRU and resume gas supply as quickly as possible, it said.
It said it is closely monitoring the gas supply situation and expressed hope that supply condition would improve once the technical problem at the FSRU is resolved.
It also apologized to consumers for the inconvenience caused by the disruption.

Ministry: Fuel shortage rumours aimed at creating panic
item.description:
The Energy and Mineral Resources Division on Wednesday alleged that rumours about a fuel shortage are being deliberately spread in an attempt to create panic and an artificial sense of crisis, insisting that the country has sufficient stocks of petroleum products and no risk of supply disruption.
Speaking at a press briefing at the Secretariat, Energy and Mineral Resources Division Spokesperson and Joint Secretary (Operations) Monir Hossain Chowdhury said recent reports published by a few media outlets regarding fuel oil and natural gas had created unnecessary confusion among the public.
"Some media outlets have published reports regarding our fuel oil and natural gas supplies. We believe it is important to present the actual situation so that people are not misled by rumours or misinformation," he said.
He said Bangladesh currently has ample fuel reserves, with diesel stocks sufficient for around 31 days, octane for 36 days, petrol for 20 days, furnace oil for 25 days and jet fuel for 20 days.
"These reserves are well above the normal operational requirement. Our supply chain remains fully functional, and there will be no problem meeting demand throughout July and August," he added.
Monir said the government is working to gradually increase the country's fuel reserve capacity to 45 days, then 60 days, and eventually to 90 days.
He also said another 180,000 tonnes of diesel are expected to arrive by July 31, while an additional 240,000 tonnes will be imported in August.
"We have adequate stocks, and there is no cause for concern. There is no shortage of any other petroleum products either," he said.

item.title: ECNEC clears 8 projects involving Tk 14,014 crore
item.description:
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday approved eight development projects involving an estimated cost of Tk 14,041.21 crore.
The approvals came at an ECNEC meeting chaired by Prime Minister and ECNEC Chairperson Tarique Rahman at secretariat.
Of the total project cost, the government will provide Tk 10,494.21 crore from its own resources while Tk 3,550.44 crore will come as project assistance.
The approved package includes three new projects and five revised ones.
Among the approved projects, three belong to the Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Ministry.
These are first revised Universal Social Infrastructure Development-2 (GSIDP-2) project, Integrated Development Project for greater Dinajpur (Dinajpur, Thakurgaon and Panchagarh) and Rural Road Maintenance and Employment Project.
The Disaster Management and Relief Ministry secured approval for the third revised Disaster Shelter Construction, Renovation and Improvement Project.
The Road Transport and Bridges Ministry received approval for Dhaka-Ashulia Elevated Expressway Construction Project (2nd revised).
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry obtained approval for two projects: Power Distribution System Development Project for Sylhet Division (3rd revision) and a project to drill one appraisal-cum-development well (Begumganj-5) and two exploratory wells (Begumganj-6 and Sunetra-2).
The Health and Family Welfare Ministry’s project (2nd revision) to upgrade existing kidney dialysis centers at medical college hospitals to 50-bed facilities and establish 10-bed dialysis centers at district hospitals was also approved.
The ECNEC meeting was also informed about 11 projects each involving less than Tk 50 crore.
These include projects related to establishing three regional offices of the National University, setting up the Barishl Textile Vocational Institute at Gournadi, installing a mobile network at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport’s Third Terminal, upgrading sections of regional and district highways, developing power transmission infrastructure for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, expanding the eastern grid network and establishing six BITAC centers in different districts.

item.title: CNG drivers block airport road over gas shortage
item.description:
CNG-run auto-rickshaw drivers blocked airport road in Dhaka's Khilkhet area on Wednesday afternoon, protesting the ongoing gas shortage and causing severe traffic congestion.
The blockade began around 2:40pm as drivers demanded an immediate solution to the gas crisis.
Monir Hossain, a protesting driver, said they had been waiting in line since morning but were unable to refill gas.
"The lack of gas is affecting our daily income and making it difficult to cover vehicle deposits and other expenses. Most of the day is spent just trying to collect gas," he said.
Witnesses said around 100 CNG drivers gathered on the road, chanting slogans and demanding an immediate resolution to the shortage.
Sub-Inspector Abul Hossain of Khilkhet Police Station said police were at the scene to keep the situation under control.
"The CNG drivers have blocked the road due to the gas shortage. Police are working to maintain order," he said.

item.title: Charge framing hearing against Anisul Huq deferred to August 23
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday deferred the charge framing hearing in an arms case against former law minister Anisul Huq to August 23.
Judge Moin Uddin Chowdhury of Dhaka's Special Tribunal-4 set the new date after the defence sought more time, citing the sudden illness of its senior counsel.
In the petition, defence lawyer Md Sumon Hossain said the appointed senior lawyer was seriously ill and unable to appear before the court, requesting additional time to avoid prejudice to the accused.
Anisul Huq was produced before the court from jail during the hearing.
According to the case statement, Anisul Huq was the licensed owner of a pistol registered under Banani Police Station. The Ministry of Home Affairs suspended all firearm licenses issued for personal security between January 6, 2009, and August 5, 2024, and instructed license holders to deposit their firearms by September 3, 2024.
The prosecution alleged that Anisul Huq failed to surrender his licensed firearm or inform the police station between September 4, 2024, and May 5, 2025. Officials also failed to locate anyone at his registered address and found no information regarding the weapon's surrender. The case statement further said there was no record of him purchasing ammunition.
Sub-inspector Md Jane Alam Dulal of Banani Police Station filed the case on May 24 last year.
Following the investigation, Sub-Inspector Md Yadul Haque of Banani Police Station submitted the charge sheet against Anisul Huq on August 29, 2025.
Anisul Huq was arrested on August 13, 2024, from the Sadarghat area while allegedly attempting to flee by waterway based on secret information. Since then, he has been remanded in several murder and attempted murder cases and remains in jail.

Dubai offers discounts to residents bringing in tourists
item.description:
Dubai will offer more than $800 worth of discounts and deals to residents who bring friends and family to visit, the emirate’s media office said on Wednesday, as months of war have battered its tourism sector.
“The Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism launches ‘A Dubai Invite,’ inviting residents to become ambassadors of the city by welcoming their loved ones to Dubai,” the Dubai media office said in a post on X, adding that the program would run until the end of October.
Summers are usually a low season for tourists in the United Arab Emirates, a mostly desert country where temperatures can reach 50°C.
The Dubai government website says residents wishing to invite friends and family to visit from July 20 to October 31 can “receive benefits worth over AED 3,000 ($816), including hotel stays, dining experiences, attraction tickets and more.”
Residents can nominate people they wish to invite on the website to enjoy the benefits.
With 19.5 million yearly tourists, Dubai is among the region’s top destinations and was long seen as a playground for the world’s rich and famous.
Although the UAE has so far not been hit in the latest round of US-Iran escalation, the war that erupted in February shattered the Gulf’s image as a haven of stability, with Tehran directing its fury at the oil-rich region.
The United Arab Emirates bore the brunt of Iran’s missiles and drones, which hit hotels, including on the Palm, as well as its landmark Burj Al Arab resort and sent tourists fleeing during the winter high season.
Since a shaky ceasefire came into effect on April 8 some tourists have trickled in, but hotels are mostly relying on local guests, people working in the industry have told AFP.
In May, the Dubai government approved an economic package worth more than $400 million to help businesses struggling to cope with the aftermath of the war and Iran’s blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.
The incentives included exemptions from municipal fees for hotels and restaurants, reduced fines for customs violations and lower fees for civil aviation permits.
In late March, Dubai authorities had announced a first package worth over $270 million to help businesses and families.
